reason: Consistency page: item stays in the DAX cache, another client updates it bypassing DAX, and both hold inconsistent values until the DAX item TTL expires; the app must anticipate and tolerate the inconsistencies.
Under 'When not to use DAX', infrequent or cold data gives a likely low cache hit ratio and the cache overhead might not justify the performance gains.
The DR strategy page states PITR provides granular recovery with minimal RPO (seconds) and reasonable RTO (minutes to hours); claim attributes it to the guide.
FAQ billing-units answer: pay only for resources consumed, scales to zero when not in use with on-demand, and while in use write and read request units calculate charges.
FAQ 'Why should I use global tables?' states both parts: resiliency across Regions and optionally accounts, and high availability if an entire Region is isolated or degraded.

PrivateLink page states the gateway endpoint route-table definition, the interface endpoint private-IP routing from VPC, on premises or another Region via peering or Transit Gateway, and that both types can be used in one VPC.
Quote says all replicas share the same table name, primary key schema, and item data; the claim states a true subset (key schema and item data) with the same scope.

Page Important note gives the 2017.11.29 (Legacy) scope; the auto scaling section says it is the recommended way for provisioned replicas; the Note gives on-demand when auto scaling does not fit or settings are unwanted.
Under 'Choosing a consistency mode', 'You should use the MREC mode when' lists that the application can tolerate stale data from strongly consistent reads updated in another Region.
Quote is the exact sentence under 'Initial throughput and scaling properties': new on-demand tables sustain up to 4,000 writes and 12,000 reads per second.

Pricing page lists on-demand as recommended in most scenarios incl. new or existing workloads with no capacity management, and provisioned may be better for existing apps with steady predictable throughput.
Scan page: RCUs are based on number and size of items, not data returned; same with all attributes or a projection expression, and same with or without a filter expression.
Provisioned mode page: RCUs are based on strongly consistent reads; each read's RCU number is item size divided by 4 KB rounded up (3 KB gives 1 RCU), in context of the strongly consistent example.

Lambda page gives synchronous invocation and up to two functions per stream; document history gives Flink via Managed Service for Apache Flink; EventBridge page gives pipe consuming Streams and routing to a bus.
Comparison table row 'Stream processing options' lists Lambda, Managed Service for Apache Flink, Firehose or Glue streaming ETL for KDS and Lambda or the Streams Kinesis adapter for DynamoDB Streams.
PERF03-BP01 states relational databases have upper bounds on provisioned storage and often must be horizontally partitioned, e.g. sharding, at those limits.
Provisioned mode page: each write needs one WCU for a 512-byte item; divide item size by 1 KB and round up, with the 512 bytes / 1 KB example.
